title: India's Home Ministry cyber agency warns officials against sharing sensitive information over WhatsApp Web
date_note: IANS's article is dated 23 November; the page gives no earlier date for the advisory.
org: Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
geo_basis: article dateline New Delhi; agency is the Union Home Ministry's
summary: According to IANS, the Union Home Ministry's cyber security agency I4C warned government officials not to share sensitive information over WhatsApp Web, saying an active session could let someone take over the account for fraud or phishing. It advises logging out after each session and avoiding public or shared computers. Separately, an unnamed official source told IANS that Pakistan-based intelligence operatives had infiltrated defence-related WhatsApp groups; the I4C statement does not mention Pakistan.
plain: India's Home Ministry cyber agency told officials to log out of WhatsApp Web after use and avoid shared computers. An unnamed official source, quoted by IANS, links the warning to spying by Pakistan-based operatives.
exec: Government staff were told an open WhatsApp Web session can let someone take over the account; an unnamed official source links this to espionage.
action: I4C advises logging out after each session or using private browsing, not leaving sessions open on shared computers, avoiding cyber cafes and public kiosks, and keeping the OS, browser and security software updated.

validation.note: Both pages read carry the same IANS report; one publisher. The Hindu BusinessLine page could not be loaded. The Pakistan link is from unnamed sources, not the I4C statement.
